fieldData.bio: Thelma John specializes in community engagement and student development within the rapidly growing esports sector. With a Bachelor's Degree with Honours in Biomedical Engineering from the University of Guelph, John brings a unique analytical approach to student services. Since 2017, she has worked in student services developing programs for groups ranging from 50 to 5,000 students, with experience spanning student housing, conduct, orientation, and academic integrity. As Esports Engagement Strategist within Student Services, John focuses on introducing students to esports career possibilities, personal growth opportunities, and community connections, with particular attention to marginalized and underrepresented groups. Her work challenges common assumptions about esports regarding status, career viability, toxicity, and representation issues. She is a member of the Sierra Leone Association of Alberta and regularly plans community events and workshops. John has extensive interview experience and is enthusiastic about media opportunities to discuss esports education, student engagement, and diversity in gaming.
fieldData.current-issues-for-commentary:
• Diversity and inclusion in gaming and esports communities
  • Addressing toxicity and harassment in online gaming environments
  • Career opportunities and professional pathways in esports
  • Student engagement strategies in post-secondary education
  • Breaking stereotypes about gaming and academic achievement
  • Building inclusive communities in competitive gaming
fieldData.name: Thelma John

fieldData.bio:
Reetu Mall is a Criminologist and Program Chair for the Justice Studies Diploma with expertise in high-risk intimate partner violence, homicide prevention, trauma-informed practice, gender-based violence, offender management, and criminal justice reform. She holds a Master of Arts in Criminal Justice, with great distinction, and a Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice from Mount Royal University.

Mall has extensive experience across multiple areas of the criminal justice system, having worked in collaboration with federal and municipal police services, Crown prosecutors,  parole and probation officers, the court system, child and family services. In British Columbia she developed and led the implementation of mandatory training for all specialized Domestic Violence RCMP officers across the province, while contributing to provincial policy initiatives. Currently, as part of the Calgary Police Anti-Racism Action Committee (ARAC), Mall works collaboratively to address systemic racism and bias in policing, contributing to discussions and initiatives on race-based data collection, use-of-force policies, protest response, police accountability, transparency, and education. She teaches a range of justice courses, including Canadian Criminal Procedure, Diversity and Criminal Justice in Canada, Criminal Law, Trauma Informed Practice, Foundation of Ethics and Justice, and Crisis Management for Law Enforcement.

Available for audio interviews and print interviews, she offers expert commentary on intimate partner violence (IPV), IPV homicide prevention, gender-based violence, criminal justice reform, trauma-informed policing, and high-risk offender management.
fieldData.current-issues-for-commentary:
• Intimate partner violence prevention and intervention strategies
  • Domestic violence homicide prevention
  • Anti-racism initiatives in Canadian policing
  • High-risk offender management and public safety
  • Trauma-informed approaches in criminal justice
  • Gender-based violence policy development and implementation
  • Canadian policing and education
  • Criminal justice reform and systemic bias
fieldData.name: Reetu Mall

fieldData.bio: Stan Peake is a serial entrepreneur, bestselling business author, and TEDx speaker who brings extensive real-world experience to entrepreneurship development at Bow Valley College. As a 9-time entrepreneur and 7-time bestselling business author, Peake has been recognized as semi-finalist for both Calgary Chamber of Commerce Small Business of the Year and Better Business Bureau Ethical Business of the Year awards. His educational credentials include a graduate certificate in Values-Based Leadership from Royal Roads University, Executive Sales Leadership program from Queen's University, and Certificate in Entrepreneurship Essentials from Harvard Business School Online. As global chapter organizer for Harvard Business School Online's Entrepreneurship networking group, Peake offers expert commentary on startup ecosystems, values-based leadership, business ethics, entrepreneurship education, and small business development trends.

  • Small business challenges and recovery post-pandemic
  • Entrepreneurship education and skills development
  • Business networking strategies in digital age
  • Innovation funding and support programs for entrepreneurs

fieldData.job-title: Instructor Esports Business Management, Chiu School of Business
fieldData.bio: Shadi Hanna represents the new generation of esports education leadership, combining academic credentials with hands-on industry experience. With a BA specializing in Global & Legal Studies and Diploma in Esports Administration & Entrepreneurship, Hanna has rapidly advanced through roles including Esports Production Assistant at St. Clair College, Varsity Administrator at University of Rio Grande, and Esports Coordinator at Keyano College. His volunteer leadership includes Council Member for Esport Canada Post-Secondary and Academic Development Lead for Alberta Esports Association, while his entrepreneurial experience as President & Co-Founder of Alberta Scholastic Esports League demonstrates his commitment to growing the sector. Hanna offers fresh perspectives on esports entrepreneurship, collegiate esports development, and the business side of competitive gaming.

fieldData.bio: Mo Shaukat brings extensive frontline experience from Correctional Service Canada to his role as a Justice Studies instructor. With a Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice, Master of Public Administration, and Graduate Certificate in Financial Accounting, Shaukat's career included roles as Correctional Officer, Hostage/Crisis Negotiator, National Staff Training Officer, and Adjutant of the Guard of Honour - Prairie Region. He served as an instructor for the Canadian Armed Forces Advanced Leadership Training Program and specializes in effective communication, law and policy, de-escalation techniques, crisis management, and various security protocols. Beyond his corrections background, Shaukat founded the Alberta Chapter of Boots on the Ground, leading peer support services for first responders and military members. Currently appointed to the Policing Committee for the City of Airdrie, he offers expert commentary on corrections, crisis negotiation, first responder mental health, and justice system reform.

fieldData.bio: Ryan Coutts is a versatile entrepreneur and leadership development specialist with expertise in early-stage startups and the digital entertainment ecosystem. His diverse professional background spans motorsports, aviation, energy, and hospitality and tourism, all contributing to his unique approach to leadership and entrepreneurial mindset development. Coutts specializes in ecosystem building across film & animation, game development, and esports, with particular expertise in the esports sector. He serves as Vice President on the Board of the Alberta Esports Association and represents Alberta on the National Competitive Council for Esport Canada, making him an ideal spokesperson for discussions about esports industry growth, entrepreneurship, and digital entertainment trends.

fieldData.bio: Roy George brings extensive industry experience and international education perspective to supply chain management education. With an MBA from the University of Ljubljana, Slovenia, and MSc in Marketing from Queen's University, plus a Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, George combines technical and business expertise. His career in the downstream oil and gas industry included roles from Operations Officer to Senior Manager, spanning supply chain management, pricing, and operations at Fortune 500 companies. Since joining Bow Valley College in 2018, he has taught comprehensive supply chain management curricula and served as Interim Program Chair for Accounting and Supply Chain Management. George holds professional certifications in Supply Chain Management (CSCP) and Project Management (PMP), and his multicultural educational background (Eastern and Western institutions) provides unique insights into global supply chain challenges. He offers expert commentary on supply chain disruptions, procurement strategies, logistics, quality management, and international trade issues.

fieldData.job-title: Manager Health Care Simulation and Technology
fieldData.bio: Roger Crowe brings a unique combination of business expertise and healthcare simulation experience to medical education. With an MBA in International Trade & Finance, BSc (Pre Med), and multiple professional certifications including CCPE, Six Sigma Black Belt Professional, and Project Management Qualified, Crowe spent 15 years in the solid organ transplant community as a Medical Science Liaison with Fujisawa, working with transplant centers across Canada. He then transitioned to 10 years with CAE Healthcare as Regional Manager, collaborating with post-secondary institutions globally and developing innovative training protocols for the US Army using Microsoft Hololens AR technology. Currently managing the simulation program for the School of Health and Wellness, Crowe has received professional media training and offers expert commentary on healthcare simulation, medical education technology, and innovative training methodologies. His community involvement includes former presidency of Willow Ridge Community Association, founding CARTOD (Communities Advocating for Responsible Transit Oriented Development), and serving as advisor to multiple Calgary city boards.

  • Healthcare technology adoption in post-secondary training

fieldData.bio: Kerry Sharples combines extensive healthcare experience with educational technology innovation as Program Chair for Medical Office Assistant and Veterinary Office Assistant programs. With a Master of Arts in Learning and Technology and career progression from healthcare aide to licensed practical nurse, unit clerk, and medical office assistant, Sharples brings authentic industry insight to healthcare education. As co-founder of educational software development company Playtheos (2nd place winner at Platform Calgary), she specializes in gamification and educational technology enhancement. Her involvement in college committees for instructional technology, extended reality, and curriculum development, along with connections to Technology Development Advisors through Alberta Innovates and Calgary post-secondary technology groups, positions her as an expert on healthcare education, educational technology innovation, gamification in learning, and industry-education partnerships.

fieldData.bio: James Cairns brings nearly two decades of cybersecurity and technology leadership experience to his role as Chief Information Security Officer. Starting at BVC in 2005 as a software developer, Cairns expanded his expertise internationally with telecommunications work in New Zealand before returning to become the College's first Database Administrator in 2013 and advancing to IT Security leadership. He holds an MBA essentials from Rotman (University of Toronto), CIO.D designation from CIO Association of Canada, and Associate C|CISO from EC-Council. Currently focusing on cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance, Cairns is highly connected in the cybersecurity community as Director at Large for Canadian Cybersecurity Network, Advisory Board Member for NKST, President of BSides Calgary Security Foundation, and member of Cloud Security Alliance councils. He regularly leads Work Integrated Learning students from the Cybersecurity program and guest speaks on emerging security challenges, making him an excellent resource for media commentary on cybersecurity threats, AI governance, privacy protection, and post-secondary cybersecurity education.

fieldData.bio: Michael Lohaus brings a comprehensive background in digital entertainment and creative leadership to his role managing the Digital Entertainment Nexus esports arena and production hub. With a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Media Arts and Digital Technologies from Alberta College of Art and Design (AUArts), Lohaus progressed from junior designer to creative director, managing in-house teams for Western Canada's largest insurance company. As an entrepreneur, he launched the first Calgary-made video game on Steam and served five years as President of the Calgary Game Developers Association. His full-stack design specialization in UX and motion design, combined with extensive community and industry connections, makes him an ideal spokesperson for video game development, film/animation industry trends, esports facility development, and Calgary's growing digital entertainment ecosystem.

fieldData.job-title: Program Chair Nursing, School of Health and Wellness
fieldData.bio: Maria Manese is a certified Healthcare Simulation Educator and nursing leader with specialized expertise in geriatrics and nursing education. With Bachelor of Science degrees in Biology and Nursing, plus a Master's in Nursing Administration and Management, Maria brings both clinical and educational excellence to her role. Her international experience includes work as RN/charge nurse at St. Luke's Medical Center in the Philippines, the first institution accredited by Joint Commission International in that country, providing valuable insights into internationally educated healthcare professionals' transition to Canadian practice. Her research has been recognized nationally, including selection as the only community college research from Canada for the Sigma International Honor Society conference. Current research focuses on virtual reality in nursing education, gaps in nursing competencies in mental health and addictions, and innovative simulation activities including mock trials for nursing ethics. As a member of the Canadian College of Health Leaders and active in Sigma International Honor Society, Maria offers expert commentary on nursing education, healthcare simulation, international healthcare professional integration, and continuing care standards.

Her focus on Indigenous education and reconciliation makes her an essential voice for media discussions about decolonizing education, Indigenous perspectives in curriculum, reconciliation in post-secondary education, and narrative-based pedagogical approaches.

fieldData.bio: Corrine Ferguson is a medical sociologist with a Master of Arts in Medical Sociology and research experience in academic integrity and student well-being. Teaching courses in Introduction to Sociology, Sociology of Aging, Health and Illness, and Death and Dying, Ferguson brings both Canadian and US research and teaching experience to her role at Bow Valley College since 2013. fieldData.bio: Dr. Lisa Beuker is a biology instructor and researcher with a PhD in Immunology and Microbiology, specializing in bacterial biofilms and human disease mechanisms. Her published research focuses on bacterial communication systems that enable infections, combining her expertise in genetics, evolution, microbiome, and immunology. With additional background in health psychology through her BSc in Psychology, Dr. Beuker brings a holistic approach to understanding the intersection of biology and human behavior. Her experience includes research with Alberta Health Services on improving patient outcomes and addressing mental health services in primary care settings. Currently teaching biology courses with emphasis on human health applications, Dr. Beuker offers expert commentary on microbiology, infectious diseases, immunology, and the connections between human behavior and health outcomes.

fieldData.bio: Dr. Ravi Inder Kaur is a sociologist with a PhD focusing on gender studies, community studies, and sociology of law, with particular expertise in law and women's issues. Before immigrating to Canada in 2020, she taught sociology at undergraduate and post-graduate levels and has continued this work at Bow Valley College for 2.5 years. Her research with the Canadian Poverty Institute addresses poverty and intersectionality, while her teaching encompasses Introduction to Sociology, Sociology of Family, Sociology of Aging, and Women and Gender Studies. Dr. Kaur has extensive knowledge of gender and family issues in Canada, Indigenous women's issues, criminal justice system challenges, intimate partner violence, and victimology. With a strong background in debate and presentation through her academic career, she confidently articulates complex social issues and is available for expert commentary on gender studies, Canadian family dynamics, social justice, and intersectional approaches to poverty and law.

fieldData.job-title: Program Chair Nursing, School of Health and Wellness
fieldData.bio: Clare Howland is a nursing education innovator and Chair of the Research Ethics Board with 15 years of direct patient care experience in adult ICU, pediatric emergency, and critical care. Currently pursuing a Master of Nursing in health education principles and simulation, she holds certification as a Certified Simulation Healthcare Educator (CHSE) from the Society for Simulation in Healthcare. Her five years as a Clinical Research Nurse for the Pediatric Emergency Research Team at Alberta Children's Hospital contributed to national changes in pediatric emergency care and province-wide improvements in infectious disease surveillance. As a national leader in VR use in nursing programs, Howland designed and operationalized the PN simulation program, developed comprehensive VR programming, and conducts research comparing simulation effectiveness. Her focus on overcoming resistance to change in healthcare and education, combined with expertise in human factors and bias in program development, makes her an ideal spokesperson for healthcare innovation, nursing simulation, virtual reality in medical education, and research ethics.

  • Healthcare simulation effectiveness and patient safety
  • Research ethics in healthcare and educational settings
  • Nursing education innovation and technology adoption

fieldData.job-title: Interim Dean of Academic Innovation and Pathways
fieldData.bio: Dr. Tony Wigglesworth is a distinguished researcher and academic leader with a PhD in Organic Chemistry, specializing in photo-responsive materials. His impressive career includes serving as a research scientist at Xerox Innovation Group, where he developed advanced materials for printed electronics and holds 47 US patents, several of which were acquired by Samsung. At Innovate Calgary, he supported the commercialization of University of Calgary research with a focus on clean technology, helping researchers spin out companies including carbon capture businesses. Currently serving as Associate Dean in the School of Technology and Academic Innovation, Dr. Wigglesworth also sits on the Board of Directors for SeeO2 Energy Inc. He helped launch the Centre of Entertainment Arts and led the Digital Entertainment Nexus OCIF proposal. A passionate advocate for AI integration in education, Dr. Wigglesworth believes in embracing technology tools in both operations and teaching. He has extensive media interview experience and is available for commentary on technology innovation, clean tech, AI in education, and academic-industry partnerships.

  • AI adoption in post-secondary education and ethical considerations
  • Patent protection and intellectual property commercialization in Canada
  • Clean technology investment and government support programs
  • University-industry collaboration and technology transfer
  • Advanced materials development for sustainable electronics
